$comment: THE WORLD — PLAN §8. One continuous terrain containing every shipped site, so the site dropdown is a camera flight rather than a page reload. This file exists because the two AOI shells MISS EACH OTHER BY 3.8 km (measured): the sites are 24.4 km apart core-to-core, and rendering both AOIs as they stand leaves a hole between them. The world shell is the union, built once, and it REPLACES both per-AOI shells at runtime.
$sitesComment: Order matters only for the switcher; the first is the default camera target. Each entry is an id in config/aoi/. Adding a third site means adding it here and re-running build_shell.py --world — the shell is the only shared asset.

shell.$comment: UNION of the two AOI shells, 63.9 x 46.8 km. Computed from config/aoi/*.json rather than typed: Oberstdorf shell 10.100-10.500 / 47.300-47.600, Tegelberg shell 10.550-10.950 / 47.400-47.720. The 0.050 deg (3.8 km) gap between them at 47.5 N is exactly what this union closes.

shellGrids.$comment: Identical to the per-AOI shells, deliberately. The band was tuned by looking at renders at Oberstdorf and carried unchanged to the Tegelberg; a union shell changes the EXTENT, not the physics of the seam. At 30 m over 63.9 x 46.8 km this is 2130 x 1558 samples and ~368k mesh vertices after 3x decimation — measured to hold a locked 60 fps alongside BOTH cores (PLAN §8: p99 19.0 ms, 0% of frames over 20 ms).

shellGeobasis.$attributionComment: The ADAPTED-DATA form, as in both AOI configs: the world shell is resampled onto a UTM grid and shifted onto the cores' vertical datum, so it is unambiguously modified.
shellGeobasis.$comment: The SAME single tile that covers each site individually also covers the union: 47-48 N, 10-11 E contains 10.10-10.95 / 47.30-47.72 entirely. So the world costs ZERO new downloads — checked before building, not assumed.

elevationRangeM.$comment: Union of the two AOI ranges (Oberstdorf 790-2260, Tegelberg 780-2080), so one colour ramp and one uint16 scaling serve the whole world.
